title: One laboratory. Many details.
text: An equipment label. A repair note. A changing status. Keeping these details connected is a practical challenge in a computer laboratory.
speaker: Narrator

title: From scattered notes
text: When records are separated, even a simple question takes longer to answer: which equipment is working, and which needs attention?
speaker: Narrator

title: LABTRACKER
text: Meet LabTracker, our native PHP and MySQL application for equipment records and maintenance tracking.
speaker: Narrator

title: 01 / A clear starting point
text: We begin with administrator sign in. The password stays hidden, and the application opens a shared workspace for managing laboratory assets.
speaker: Narrator

title: The current picture
text: The dashboard summarizes equipment conditions and active maintenance, with this month’s completed maintenance costs above. These figures come from our sample records.
speaker: Narrator

title: Navigate with context
text: Below, equipment condition and laboratory summaries add context. The sidebar navigation keeps equipment, maintenance, reference data, and accounts within reach.
speaker: Narrator

title: 02 / Give every item a record
text: Let’s follow one disposable sample. We enter its asset tag, choose its category and laboratory, and add the brand, model, and serial number.
speaker: Narrator

title: Saved. Ready to inspect.
text: After saving, LabTracker confirms that the equipment was added. The detail page brings the stored information together in one readable record.
speaker: Narrator

title: Find the same record
text: Next, we search for the sample asset tag. The matching row gives us direct access to viewing, editing, and deleting that equipment.
speaker: Narrator

title: Details in one place
text: Opening View lets us check the saved details before making a change. We are following the same item throughout this demonstration.
speaker: Narrator

title: A meaningful update
text: Suppose an inspection finds a flickering screen. We change the condition to Defective and add an inspection note, then save the updated record.
speaker: Narrator

title: The change is saved
text: The detail page now shows the new condition and note. This verifies that the edit was stored.
speaker: Narrator

title: Remove only the disposable sample
text: Finally, we delete this disposable sample. The application asks for confirmation, protects equipment with maintenance history, and returns to the equipment list.
speaker: Narrator

title: 03 / Connect the repair work
text: For maintenance, we use our retained sample item. A repair entry connects the reported issue and date directly to the selected equipment.
speaker: Narrator

title: Equipment and repair stay linked
text: Saving an open repair marks this item Under Repair. The equipment list and maintenance entry describe two parts of the same situation.
speaker: Narrator

title: Record the resolution
text: After the sample repair, we select Done, enter a completion date, choose Working after verification, and describe the resolution. The saved record preserves what was reported and completed.
speaker: Narrator

title: 04 / Accounts with clear feedback
text: Administrators can also manage accounts. Here, a deliberately weak sample password is rejected with specific guidance about the requirements.
speaker: Narrator

title: Create a sample technician
text: We correct the password and create a disposable technician account. Passwords remain masked during entry, and the account list shows its role and status.
speaker: Narrator

title: Control account availability
text: We edit the sample account’s name, then deactivate it. Its status changes, preventing continued access while keeping the account record.
speaker: Narrator

title: 05 / Look beneath the interface
text: The source uses PHP password hashing and password verification. Protected pages require a session, and account activity is checked again on each request.
speaker: Narrator

title: Checks in the request path
text: Database operations use prepared statements. Server-side validation checks submitted values, while CSRF tokens are checked on form requests. These are specific implementation details.
speaker: Narrator

title: Five tables. Connected records.
text: The schema links equipment to laboratories and categories. Maintenance records reference equipment and the reporting user, connecting asset information with recorded work.
speaker: Narrator

title: Access checked after logout
text: We also test the behavior: after logout, opening the equipment page redirects to sign in. The earlier invalid password was rejected before account creation.
speaker: Narrator

title: Records → maintenance → administration
text: From creating and finding equipment to recording repairs and managing accounts, LabTracker brings these everyday laboratory tasks into a consistent workflow.
speaker: Narrator

title: The people behind the project
text: The people behind the project. Jacinth Dhane Mendoza, main developer. Jerico Teologo, interface and user experience design. Shena May Gadon, database design and data management.
speaker: Narrator

title: LABTRACKER
text: LabTracker. From equipment records to organized maintenance.
speaker: Narrator
